summary.en: Use the **comparative** to compare two things (_cheaper than_, _more interesting than_) and the **superlative** for the top or bottom of a group (_the cheapest_, _the most interesting_). Short adjectives take **-er / -est**; long ones take **more / most**. Use **as … as** for equality and **not as … as** for a lower level.
summary.es: Después del comparativo se usa than («que»), no that ni as: taller than me. Y «el más… de» se dice the most … in/of.

form: One syllable: **-er / -est** (_older, the oldest_); double the final consonant in _big → bigger_; _-y → -ier_ (_easier_)
Two or more syllables: **more / most** + adjective (_more reliable, the most reliable_)
Irregular: _good → better → the best_; _bad → worse → the worst_; _far → further_
**as + adjective + as**; **not as / not so … as**; **the + comparative, the + comparative** (_The sooner, the better_)
Modifiers: **much / far / a bit / slightly** + comparative

uses.text: **Compare two things**: _This route is **shorter than** the motorway._
**Superlative**: _the highest mountain **in** Europe_; use **in** with places and groups, **of** with a period or a number (_the best of the three_).
**Equality**: _She's **as tall as** her father._ **Difference**: _The train isn't **as fast as** a plane._

note.en: Use than after a comparative, as after as + adjective.
note.es: Than va con comparativo; as … as con igualdad.

uses.text: **Gradual change**: _Prices are getting **higher and higher**._ _The more I practise, the more confident I feel._
**Adverbs** follow the same rules: _She drives **more carefully than** me._ _He worked **the hardest** of all._

mistakes.wrong: My brother is more tall than me.
mistakes.right: My brother is taller than me.

why.es: Los adjetivos cortos usan -er, no more.

mistakes.wrong: This exam was more difficult that the last one.
mistakes.right: This exam was more difficult than the last one.

why.en: Use than, not that, after a comparative.
why.es: Después del comparativo se usa than.

mistakes.wrong: It's the most big city in the country.
mistakes.right: It's the biggest city in the country.

why.en: Big is short, so the superlative is -est: the biggest.
why.es: Big es corto: the biggest, no the most big.

mistakes.wrong: She is the best student of the class.
mistakes.right: She is the best student in the class.

why.en: Use in with a group or place: in the class, in the world.
why.es: «De la clase» se dice in the class.

examples.en: Flying is faster than going by coach, but it's more expensive.
examples.es: Volar es más rápido que ir en autocar, pero es más caro.

examples.en: This is the most comfortable chair I've ever sat in.
examples.es: Esta es la silla más cómoda en la que me he sentado.

examples.en: He isn't as patient as his sister.
The weather is getting worse and worse.
The sooner we leave, the earlier we'll arrive.
She speaks more fluently than she did last year.
It was by far the best concert of the year.
My new flat is slightly smaller than the old one.
Of all the candidates, he was the least experienced.

practice.prompt: Today is ___ than yesterday, so take a coat.

explanation.en: Cold is short, so the comparative is colder.

practice.prompt: It's the ___ restaurant in the whole city.

explanation.en: Expensive is long and the sentence needs a superlative: the most expensive.

practice.prompt: Her flat is as big ___ mine.
My English is getting ___ every month.

explanation.en: Better and better shows gradual improvement.
